questions.stem: What is the SI unit of density?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of density is kg/m^3, not g/cm^3 or pressure units.
questions.hint: SI density is kg per cubic meter.

questions.learningObjective: Define pressure as force over area
questions.stem: Pressure is defined as force divided by what quantity?
questions.explanation: Pressure equals force per unit area, not volume or mass.

questions.topic: Pressure depends on height not shape
questions.stem: In a fluid at rest, pressure at a given depth depends on what?

options.text: Depth and fluid density, not container shape.
The surface area of the fluid.

questions.explanation: Hydrostatic pressure depends on depth and density, independent of container shape.

questions.stem: Pascal's principle says a pressure change in an enclosed fluid is?
questions.explanation: Pascal's principle states pressure changes transmit undiminished throughout an enclosed fluid.

questions.stem: Archimedes' principle states buoyant force equals what?
questions.explanation: Buoyant force equals the weight of the fluid displaced by the object.

questions.topic: Density ratio decides float, suspend or sink
questions.learningObjective: Use density ratio to predict float
questions.stem: An object with density less than the fluid will do what?
questions.explanation: Lower density than the fluid means the object floats.

questions.topic: Floating body displaces its own weight
questions.stem: A floating body displaces fluid whose weight equals what?
questions.explanation: For a floating body, displaced fluid weight equals the body's weight.

questions.topic: Floating level in fresh and salt water
questions.learningObjective: Compare floating in fresh vs salt water
questions.stem: A ship floats higher in salt water than in fresh water because?

options.text: Salt water is denser, so less volume is displaced.
Fresh water has higher buoyant force.
Salt water is heavier per volume but ships sink more.

questions.explanation: Higher density salt water provides more buoyancy per volume, so less is displaced.

questions.stem: Convert 1 g/cm^3 to kg/m^3.
questions.explanation: 1 g/cm^3 equals 1000 kg/m^3.

questions.learningObjective: Compute pressure from force and area
questions.stem: A force of 200 N acts on an area of 0.5 m^2; what is the pressure in Pa?

questions.topic: Pressure depends on height not shape
questions.stem: What is the pressure at 2 m depth in water of density 1000 kg/m^3? Use g = 9.8 m/s^2.

questions.learningObjective: Apply Pascal's principle to hydraulic lift
questions.stem: A hydraulic lift multiplies force because?

options.text: Energy is created in the fluid.
Pressure is the same, but area differs.

questions.explanation: Equal pressure over different areas yields different forces.

questions.stem: A submerged object displaces 0.05 m^3 of water of density 1000 kg/m^3; what is the buoyant force in N? Use g = 9.8.
questions.explanation: Buoyant force = rho V g = 1000*0.05*9.8 = 490 N.

questions.topic: Density ratio decides float, suspend or sink
questions.stem: An object denser than the fluid will?
questions.explanation: Higher density than the fluid causes sinking.

questions.topic: Floating body displaces its own weight
questions.stem: A 500 N block floats in water of density 1000 kg/m^3; what volume in m^3 is displaced? Use g = 9.8.

options.text: 0.051 m^3, dividing weight by rho g.

questions.explanation: Displaced volume = weight/(rho g) = 500/(1000*9.8) = 0.051 m^3.

questions.topic: Floating level in fresh and salt water
questions.stem: A ship moves from fresh water to salt water; what happens to its draft?

options.misconception: thinks salt water is less dense

questions.explanation: Denser salt water means less displaced volume, so the ship rides higher.

questions.stem: Why is kg/m^3 preferred over g/cm^3 in SI calculations?

answer.exemplar: SI base units are kilograms and meters, so density in kg/m^3 keeps equations dimensionally consistent without extra conversion factors.

questions.explanation: Using base SI units avoids conversion factors and keeps physical equations consistent.

questions.stem: Two blocks have the same weight but different contact areas; which has higher pressure?

options.text: The one with larger contact area.
The one with smaller contact area.

questions.explanation: Same force over smaller area gives larger pressure.

questions.topic: Pressure depends on height not shape
questions.stem: Why does pressure at the bottom of a wide container equal that in a narrow one at the same depth?

answer.exemplar: Hydrostatic pressure depends only on depth and fluid density, so container shape and total fluid volume do not affect the pressure at a given level.

questions.explanation: Pressure at depth depends on fluid column above, not on container width.

questions.stem: Car brakes work on which principle?

options.text: Pascal's principle in enclosed brake fluid.

questions.explanation: Brake fluid transmits pressure equally to all wheel cylinders.

questions.stem: A ship floats because?

options.text: It is lighter than water overall.
It contains air, so no water is displaced.
It displaces water whose weight equals the ship's weight.

questions.explanation: Floating occurs when displaced water weight balances the ship's weight.

questions.topic: Density ratio decides float, suspend or sink
questions.stem: An object has density 1000 kg/m^3 and fluid density is 1000 kg/m^3; what is its state?
questions.explanation: Equal densities mean neutral buoyancy; the encoded value 0 represents suspended state (no net force).

questions.topic: Floating body displaces its own weight
questions.stem: Why does a floating body not sink further into the fluid?

answer.exemplar: As it sinks deeper it displaces more fluid, increasing buoyant force until that force equals the body's weight and equilibrium is reached.

questions.explanation: Deeper displacement increases buoyant force until it matches the body's weight.

questions.topic: Floating level in fresh and salt water
questions.learningObjective: Compute floating fraction in salt water
questions.stem: A block of density 800 kg/m^3 floats in salt water of density 1000 kg/m^3; what fraction is submerged?

options.text: 0.8, dividing object density by fluid density.

questions.explanation: Submerged fraction = rho_object/rho_fluid = 800/1000 = 0.8.

questions.learningObjective: Compute density from mass and volume
questions.stem: A 2 kg object occupies 0.001 m^3; what is its density in kg/m^3?
questions.explanation: Density = mass/volume = 2/0.001 = 2000 kg/m^3.

questions.stem: A force of 5000 N acts on 0.25 m^2; what is the pressure in kPa?

questions.topic: Pressure depends on height not shape
questions.stem: The pressure difference between two points 3 m apart vertically in water of density 1000 kg/m^3 is how many Pa? Use g = 9.8.
questions.explanation: Delta P = rho g h = 1000*9.8*3 = 29400 Pa.

questions.learningObjective: Compute output force in hydraulic system
questions.stem: In a hydraulic lift, input area 0.01 m^2 has 100 N; output area 0.5 m^2. What is output force in N?
An object displaces 0.02 m^3 of water of density 1000 kg/m^3; what mass of water is displaced in kg?
questions.explanation: Mass = rho V = 1000*0.02 = 20 kg.

questions.topic: Density ratio decides float, suspend or sink
questions.stem: An object with the same density as the fluid will?
questions.explanation: Equal densities produce neutral buoyancy.

questions.topic: Floating body displaces its own weight
questions.stem: A wooden block of density 600 kg/m^3 floats in water of density 1000 kg/m^3; what fraction is submerged?
questions.explanation: Submerged fraction = 600/1000 = 0.6.

questions.topic: Floating level in fresh and salt water
questions.learningObjective: Compute displaced volume in salt water
questions.stem: A 10000 N ship floats in salt water of density 1025 kg/m^3; what volume in m^3 is displaced? Use g = 9.8.

options.text: 0.995 m^3, dividing weight by rho g.

questions.learningObjective: State density of water in SI
questions.stem: What is the approximate density of water in SI units?
questions.explanation: Water's density is about 1000 kg/m^3 in SI units.

questions.stem: Why does pressure at a point in a fluid not depend on the container shape?

answer.exemplar: Pressure at a point depends only on the weight of the fluid column above it, so the horizontal shape or width of the container does not change that vertical column.

questions.explanation: Only the vertical fluid column above the point determines pressure.

questions.topic: Pressure depends on height not shape
questions.stem: At 1 m and 3 m depths in the same water, which pressure is greater?
questions.explanation: Greater depth means greater hydrostatic pressure.

questions.stem: Pascal's principle requires the fluid to be?
questions.explanation: Pascal's principle applies to enclosed, static fluids.

questions.stem: Buoyant force is a result of?

options.text: Pressure difference between top and bottom of object.

questions.explanation: Pressure is greater at the bottom than the top, creating net upward buoyant force.

questions.learningObjective: Compute density from mass and volume
questions.stem: An object of mass 3 kg and volume 0.002 m^3 has what density in kg/m^3?

questions.topic: Floating body displaces its own weight
questions.stem: A 20000 N boat floats; how many newtons of water does it displace?
questions.explanation: Floating means displaced water weight equals boat weight, 20000 N.

questions.topic: Floating level in fresh and salt water
questions.learningObjective: Compare buoyant force in different fluids
questions.stem: For the same submerged volume, buoyant force is greater in?

options.text: Both are equal regardless of density.

questions.explanation: Buoyant force = rho_fluid V g, so denser fluid gives larger buoyant force.

questions.stem: Convert 2500 kg/m^3 to g/cm^3.
questions.explanation: Divide by 1000: 2500 kg/m^3 = 2.5 g/cm^3.

questions.learningObjective: Compute pressure at depth in oil
questions.stem: What is the pressure at 1.5 m depth in oil of density 800 kg/m^3? Use g = 9.8. Answer in Pa.
How can a small force lift a heavy load in a hydraulic system?

answer.exemplar: A small force on a small piston creates pressure that is transmitted equally to a larger piston, where the same pressure acts over a larger area to produce a larger force.

questions.explanation: Equal pressure over larger area yields larger force.

questions.learningObjective: Compute buoyant force in different fluid
questions.stem: An object displaces 0.01 m^3 of oil of density 800 kg/m^3; what is the buoyant force in N? Use g = 9.8.
questions.explanation: Buoyant force = 800*0.01*9.8 = 78.4 N.

questions.topic: Density ratio decides float, suspend or sink
questions.stem: An object of density 500 kg/m^3 placed in water of density 1000 kg/m^3 will?
questions.explanation: Lower density than water means the object floats.

questions.topic: Floating body displaces its own weight
questions.stem: Why does a floating body displace exactly its own weight of fluid?

answer.exemplar: At equilibrium the upward buoyant force must balance the downward weight of the body, and buoyant force equals the weight of displaced fluid.

questions.explanation: Equilibrium requires buoyant force to equal body weight, and buoyant force equals displaced fluid weight.

questions.topic: Floating level in fresh and salt water
questions.stem: A hydrometer floats in both water and alcohol; in which does it sit lower?

options.text: In water, because water is less dense.
At the same level in both.
In alcohol, because alcohol is less dense.

questions.explanation: Less dense alcohol requires more displaced volume, so the hydrometer sits lower.

questions.stem: A metal sample has mass 8.9 kg and volume 0.001 m^3; what is its density in kg/m^3?
Surface X has 100 N over 0.5 m^2; surface Y has 80 N over 0.2 m^2. Which has higher pressure?

options.text: Surface Y at 400 Pa, higher than X at 200 Pa.

questions.explanation: X = 200 Pa, Y = 400 Pa, so Y is higher.

questions.topic: Pressure depends on height not shape
questions.stem: What is the absolute pressure at 10 m depth in water? Use rho = 1000, g = 9.8, atmospheric = 101325 Pa.
questions.explanation: Absolute = atmospheric + rho g h = 101325 + 98000 = 199325 Pa.

questions.stem: A car jack lifts a heavy car with a small hand force because?

options.text: Gravity is reduced in the fluid.
Force is conserved in the fluid.
Pressure transmits equally and area is larger on the load side.

questions.explanation: Equal pressure over larger area produces larger force on the car.
